content: Penicillin G procaine is a component of Bicillin C-R, an injectable suspension that contains equal amounts of penicillin G benzathine and penicillin G procaine salts. This formulation is specifically designed for deep intramuscular injection. Penicillin G benzathine is synthesized through the reaction of dibenzylethylenediamine with two molecules of penicillin G. Chemically, it is designated as (2S, 5R, 6R)-3,3-Dimethyl-7-oxo-6-(2-phenylacetamido)-4-thia-1-azabicycloheptane-2-carboxylic acid combined with N,N'-dibenzylethylenediamine in a 2:1 molar ratio, and it exists as a tetrahydrate. This compound appears as a white, crystalline powder that is very slightly soluble in water and sparingly soluble in alcohol. Penicillin G procaine, on the other hand, is an equimolar salt of procaine and penicillin G. Its chemical designation is (2S, 5R, 6R)-3,3-Dimethyl-7-oxo-6-(2-phenylacetamido)-4-thia-1-azabicycloheptane-2-carboxylic acid combined with 2-(diethylamino)ethyl p-aminobenzoate in a 1:1 molar ratio, existing as a monohydrate. It appears as white crystals or a white, microcrystalline powder and is slightly soluble in water. The Bicillin C-R injectable suspension, when provided in a disposable syringe formulation, is viscous and opaque in appearance. It is important to review the CONTRAINDICATIONS, WARNINGS, PRECAUTIONS, and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION sections thoroughly before administering this medication.
